column1: # Chat spellings of common Malayalam words that no general rule reaches: latin<TAB>malayalam.
# Hand-written for this repository; see data/manifests/chat-forms.json. The Malayalam pack's
# "chatForms" file, read by the engine (engine/core/src/chat_forms.rs). A typed word matching a
# row (ignoring case) offers its Malayalam word as if the letters spelled it out.
# Only genuinely irregular forms belong here. Before adding a row, check that the skeleton
# lookup and the transliterator don't already reach the word, and that the irregularity is
# specific to the word rather than a rule (a rule belongs in romanize.rs). Measured on the
# Dakshina romanisation lexicon (Google Research, ml.translit.sampled.*): of 843 romanisations
# of words with ന്ദ, only നന്ദി and നന്ദിയുടെ were written with "nn"; 784 used "nd". So the
# spoken nd -> nn of നന്ദി is a property of that word, not a spelling rule.
# നന്ദി (thank you), said and typed "nanni". User-reported on device, 2026-11-03.
nanni
# എന്റെ / എന്താ / എന്ത് with the initial vowel dropped, as in chat ("nte veedu", "ntha?").
# The skeleton lookup reads these as the fragment tokens ന്റെ and ന്ത from the corpus.
nte
nde
ntha
nthu
# പൊളി (great, slang), spelled "pwoli": the w marks the rounded o of the spoken word.
pwoli
pwolichu
